truths.truth: SUMMARY's post-review claim holds: a COMPLETE tracker miss overrules a confirmed FILED.md row only on github, the one forge whose query was measured.
truths.evidence: Tested rather than accepted. lookupMeasured is a per-row frozen fact - true on github (filing-decision.mjs:704), false on forgejo (:676) and gitlab (:727) - and is read at exactly one site, issue-filing.mjs:844, gating only the MISS arm. Named tests pass: filing-decision 'only the row whose lookup was RUN is marked measured' (and every row's flag is a boolean, so a new row reads unmeasured by omission); issue-filing 'on a forge whose lookup is UNMEASURED, a complete miss cannot overrule a confirmed row' (forgejo, listBody '[]', confirmed row for FIVE[0]: 1 create of FIVE[2] only, suppressed on FILED.md, ledger_stood_in true, and the `issues list` child did run - not the child-failed arm); 'an unmeasured forge still honours a lookup HIT' (suppressed by number 12, authority 'tracker', ledger_stood_in false); and the github control 'a fingerprint FILED.md already carries gets no SECOND row, even when it is re-filed' (complete miss on github DOES create over the confirmed row, leaving one row). CONTEXT.md D-04 carries the correction inline.

truths.truth: On forgejo and gitlab, the shipped lookup query actually returns an issue whose title carries the fingerprint - so the phase goal's 'never re-filed blind' holds on those two forges and not only on github.
truths.evidence: The two arms space-join their tokens because neither CLI offers an OR - filing-decision.mjs:696 (`--keyword <tokens joined by space>`, tea) and :746 (`--search <tokens joined by space> --in title`, glab) - and whether either matches a bracketed hex token in a title, or reads a space-joined string as more than one term, is written into those rows' own comments as ASSUMED, NOT MEASURED. Nothing in this checkout can settle it: the argv is pinned byte-exact and the pinned vector test passes either way. The blast radius is bounded by truth 8 (an unmeasured miss never overrules the ledger) but not closed: a fingerprint the tracker holds with NO FILED.md row - one of D-04's nine pre-phase orphans, or an issue filed from another checkout - can still be created a second time on those two forges. This is the open item SUMMARY.md:66-73 declares, and it is the reason SUMMARY's own goal check says the 'never' is measured on github and assumed elsewhere.

human_checks.name: Run the forgejo and gitlab lookup queries against a live instance that holds an issue whose title carries a known Cadence fingerprint: `tea issues list --repo <slug> --login <login> --keyword '<fp1> <fp2>' --state all --fields index,title --output json --limit 50` and `glab issue list --repo <slug> --search '<fp1> <fp2>' --in title --all --output json --per-page 100`. If the issue comes back, flip that row's `lookupMeasured` to true in cadence-core/bin/lib/filing-decision.mjs and replace its ASSUMED comment with the measurement; if it does not, the join spelling in that row's `lookup` builder is what has to change.
human_checks.expected: Each query returns the issue whose title carries the fingerprint, and a two-token query returns both - which is what makes an empty answer on those forges real evidence of a miss rather than a query that matched nothing.
human_checks.why_human: Out-of-reach resource, not an unexercised path: settling it needs a live Forgejo and a live GitLab instance already holding an issue whose title carries a Cadence fingerprint. No such instance exists in this environment, the check is a network call this verification may not make, and no stub can answer it - a stub would only replay the assumption. The github arm was measured live on 2026-09-03 and is the reason that row alone carries lookupMeasured: true.
